report:
R1
- Behavior: Replace the hard-coded `EXPECTED_POST_CUTOFF` basename comparison with one oracle that classifies candidates from the sealed cutoff: frozen construction identity membership plus the sealed discovery predicates/filesystem boundaries and exact candidate identity. The live walk must be partitioned all-and-only against that rule; a basename alone must never establish post-cutoff status.
- Deepest Owner: `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, specifically the fixed-target construction-walk test and its local sealed-predicate/candidate-identity helpers.
- Red: Feed the same oracle a synthetic omitted frozen/pre-cutoff identity whose basename is `coder.ts`; assert rejection. This counterexample must fail the former basename allowlist while exercising the production assertion path, not a parallel helper.
- Green: The real source root yields 597 matched, 0 missing, 0 changed and an exact cutoff-derived partition; every accepted addition carries identity evidence showing it is absent from the sealed pre-cutoff identity set, while the synthetic omitted pre-cutoff `coder.ts` is rejected.
- Scope: Modify only the existing verifier for this regression. Do not add another verifier/helper, recut the denominator, inspect payloads, or alter frozen migration evidence.

R2
- Behavior: Build a deterministic recursive association extractor over frozen item metadata and every admitted non-generic source byte. Traverse nested JSON values and Markdown/text, recognize issue/PR references and full/uniquely resolvable commit identities (including fields such as `reviewedHead` and `commitOid`), and include referenced Git bytes as well as recovered/external bytes. Explicitly gate generic JSONL/session/tool-event items before any semantic read. Compare canonical sorted/deduplicated exact sets against both disposition and recovered-index metadata, then update those two migration metadata owners to the newly derived exact values.
- Deepest Owner: The association oracle in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`; persisted association facts remain owned by `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/dispositions.json` and `.ak/dockets/issues/15/migration/legacy-case-a/recovered-index.json`.
- Red: Clone the actual parsed record/input for the second known item (`33454566…`), mutate its real `issuePrCommitAssociations` field (or the parsed admitted input that derives it), and pass that mutated record through the identical canonical exact-set comparator; assert the mismatch. Retain a corresponding first-item check so both actual metadata paths are covered. Do not simulate failure by deleting an expected-map entry.
- Green: The oracle derives one stable exact association set from all eligible frozen metadata/recovered/reference bytes; every persisted field equals it exactly, nested JSON and Markdown/text examples are represented, and both actual-field mutations fail. No excluded generic payload is opened.
- Scope: Change the existing verifier plus only association fields in the two current migration metadata files. Do not alter source/derivative bytes, reports, generic payload policy, or unrelated migration facts.

R3
- Behavior: Append a new repair-003 Recorder closure containing one independently executable child, its result, and a manifest/identity ledger. The child must independently rerun the corrected cutoff oracle and invoke real `scanBytes`; selection, dispositions, derivatives, and reports must come from immutable Git inputs. Before importing/executing the scanner, resolve and verify its exact bytes. Record repository identity/full commit/path/blob OID/SHA-256 for every Git-resolvable discovery spec, walk, inventory, disposition, report, scanner, derivative, and other repository input; for each genuinely external source record item key, source SHA-256, and applicable frozen identity metadata only.
- Deepest Owner: A new `.ak/dockets/issues/15/repair/repair-003/recorder-closure/` manifest with stored executable exhibit and summary/ledger input; the child itself owns execution gates, while the manifest owns immutable attribution.
- Red: In the child’s own assertion path, perturb representative ledger tuple components, scanner hash, selection identity, source seal, complete hit report, cutoff identity, and each of the two known-redacted records and require nonzero/failure; mechanically exercise these checks from the sole verifier against the stored successor evidence.
- Green: A clean child exits 0 only with 597/0/0 identities, cutoff-derived all-and-only partition, exactly 277 selected sources, verified scanner bytes, matching source and derivative hashes, exact complete hit reports, and both redactions. The ledger is complete and every tuple/seal resolves and hashes correctly; no raw external source duplicate is stored.
- Scope: Append only the new successor. Preserve repair-002 manifest, exhibit and result byte-for-byte (current SHA-256 seals `fd219ea9e1d43aae383d67a0289a92612726980e62b6a1aaf97fdacb19411576` and `654fdff4002b26cdaf08586b722aff6688b8c19b08752a62d329a84ef40e9a70`) and preserve all earlier evidence. Do not share implementation with the seam verifier or retain scratch probes.

R4
- Behavior: Extend the sole verifier to mechanically resolve every successor Git tuple, verify every external seal/frozen metadata binding, verify the corrected association exact sets and real red mutations, and enforce preservation of all historical evidence at the forward target.
- Deepest Owner: Acceptance assertions in `test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`, backed by the repository’s `typecheck` script and the new Recorder successor’s exit/result gates.
- Red: Each tuple/seal mutation, association-field mutation, historical blob/hash mutation, repair-002 seal mutation, source-count drift, source identity loss/change, scanner drift, incomplete hit report, missing redaction, or non-forward target must make the focused verifier or child fail. If application discovers any required historical or external identity missing/changed, stop with evidence-bearing refusal rather than substituting a cutoff or denominator.
- Green: Run `npm run typecheck` and `node --import tsx --test test/legacy-case-a-migration-verifier.test.ts`; both pass at the new forward descendant. The successor child records exit 0, all ledger checks pass, the four immutable commits remain ancestors, the four Receipt/manifest blob+SHA identities in `historical-nonconformance.json` re-resolve unchanged, and the two repair-002 seals remain exact. Baseline investigation already found a clean tree, 597 construction identities, the existing focused suite passing 17/17, and both repair-002 seals intact.
- Scope: Verification and preservation only: no changes to prior migration source bytes, repair/Receipt/manifest/exhibit/result/historical-nonconformance evidence, no history rewrite, no Case B or issues 16/17, no session retention, no generic/excluded-payload inspection, and no Soul/runtime/schema work.
